children: Chief Executive Bezalel Machlis expects reduced U.S. military aid to Israel to encourage local weapons production and create export opportunities. He said Israeli manufacturers could supply products currently purchased from American companies under aid spending requirements.
For investors, that potential comes with funding and collection risks. Israel’s Defense Ministry generated more than a third of Elbit’s
revenue through September, and payment delays remain unresolved. Greater domestic procurement could support orders, but pressure on government finances could complicate their conversion into cash.

The existing agreement provides Israel with $3.8 billion annually through 2028. President Donald Trump’s announcement that assistance would end soon has clouded future funding, while Israel’s Finance Ministry says $31 billion in orders depend on U.S. aid. Machlis nevertheless expects Elbit’s projects to continue.
